content.text:
I submitted **index 1** (Fe 0.857, Sb 0.143, Sb-doped hematite) as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.228%, the highest of the three I measured. That was the whole merit budget; I used none of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Fe : Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | 0.507 : 0.493 (FeSbO4) | 0.018 |
| 1 | 0.857 : 0.143 | **0.228** |
| 0 | 0.878 : 0.122 | 0.141 |

- **Index 13:** I measured the 1:1 composition first because the models looked good for it. MACE puts rutile FeSbO4 on the convex hull (stable), and MEGNet predicts a gap of about 2.1 eV, below the 3.2 eV illumination. It still performed poorly.
- **Index 1:** I moved to the Fe-rich end next. MEGNet gives hematite a gap of about 2.8 eV, and MACE puts the Sb-rich FeSb2O4 phase 0.18 eV/atom above the hull (unlikely to form). EQE rose more than tenfold.
- **Index 0:** I spent the last measurement on the most Fe-rich film, expecting the trend to continue, but EQE dropped to 0.141%. That points to an optimum at around 14% Sb.

The main uncertainty is that index 1 is just a peak among three points. Films with somewhat more Sb (indices 2–4, about 16–24% Sb) were never measured, and the Gaussian-process model's top pick was index 5 at about 25% Sb. So the library's true best could be in that range and I can't rule it out.
